newsitem.title: USA: L.A. County board accepts $11.9 bln budget plan.
newsitem.headline: L.A. County board accepts $11.9 bln budget plan.

text.p: The Los Angeles County Board of Supervisors took the first step on Tuesday toward approving an $11.97 billion 1997/1998 budget proposal that calls for 1,200 job cuts in the health services department.

The board voted five-zero to adopt the proposal, marking the beginning of the budget review process. The board will hold budget hearings in May before the supervisors begin their final deliberations. The 1997/1998 budget year begins July 1.
Los Angeles County's chief administrative officer on Monday proposed the $11.97 billion spending plan.
County CAO David Janssen said his proposed spending plan -- $173 million smaller than the current budget -- was balanced, but warned that the county's financial condition remained "precarious."
Janssen's budget proposal included an operating reserve of $29.7 million.

The budget called for the loss of an estimated 1,200 positions in the county Health Services Department due to downsizing. The county would add, however, hundreds of social service and sheriff's department jobs, Janssen said.

The budget included 304 new positions in the department of public social services to help welfare recipients find jobs and 718 new sheriff's department jobs for the county's Twin Towers jail in downtown Los Angeles.
Janssen warned that several factors could undermine his budget plan, including fluctuations in state funding and unexpected costs associated with welfare reform.
The budget does not include any funds for pay raises. Most county employees have not had a raise for three years, and for many groups it has been four and five years.
